high_precision_recheck.method: 100-decimal monotone bisection around chi-square/normal quantiles using arbitrary-precision incomplete-gamma/erf evaluation. This supplies very tight numerical brackets and sign-residual checks but is not a formally directed-rounding interval proof because the transcendental evaluator itself was not interval-certified.
high_precision_recheck.result: All r82 float64 constants agree to displayed double precision. Symbolic monotonicity and algebra are unchanged. True machine-verified interval arithmetic remains open.

matched_simulation.scope: P=N(0,1), fixed iid Gaussian step alternatives on the exact D_KL(Q||P)=1 boundary; 11 directions spanning both pure-variance endpoints, low/high mixed variance, pure mean with both signs, and intermediate mixed directions. Same reference/null-prefix/post-change Gaussian randomness was reused across compared detectors and KL directions within each path. Engineering evidence only; theorem-level PFA claims remain those of the source constructions.

detector_r82_hybrid.description: r82 four-direction common-increment delayed-start block e-process, with variance blocks m=8, mean blocks m=32, equal direction weights. The first-start r77 t/F sentinel keeps its original tiny alpha_start=0.0001845351232142713; the r82 conditional e-process level is reduced from 0.03 to 0.029815464876785727 so 0.02 reference-failure union + sentinel + e-process remains <=0.05.

detector_r81.description: r81 raw identity-score conditional CTM at alpha=0.01/delta=0.01 plus Gaussian variance-CI p-to-e increase/decrease channels at alpha=0.01 each and variance-CI failure 0.01, total union budget <=0.05. Fixed power calibrators kappa_up=0.49955, kappa_down=0.47569.

null_smoke.interpretation: Finite smoke test only; it is not the source of either PFA guarantee.

change_results.interpretation: r81 retains a small immediate-change latency edge on the tested KL=1 grid, especially mean-dominated directions.
The common-increment delayed-start mixture is already materially better once change is delayed.
The start-at-monitoring wealth route can become effectively bankrupt before a late variance change; the delayed-start mixture does not.

At a very late step the r82 delay rises only modestly on this grid, consistent with the logarithmic start-weight penalty, while the r81 start-at-monitoring route loses both speed and endpoint power within the finite horizon.

sentinel_ablation.interpretation: On this tested immediate KL=1 grid the r77 sentinel adds little empirical latency benefit; its main retained value is finite-sample analytic first-start certification over the unbounded KL>=1 class rather than average speed.

tuning_screen.candidate: mean block m=16 with per-variance-direction weight 0.20 and per-mean-direction weight 0.30
tuning_screen.engineering_effect_at_prechange_10000: some mean-dominated q90 values improved from 144 to 128 raw samples while variance directions were nearly unchanged
tuning_screen.formal_counterweight: the conservative component-only 95% mean delay bound worsens at late starts because halving block size doubles the start index and therefore the heavy-tail pi_k penalty; at prechange 1e6, m32/w0.25 gives 2400 raw vs m16/w0.30 gives 2448 raw
tuning_screen.decision: do not adopt tuning yet; current m32 equal-weight design keeps the stronger existing formal certificate.

new_public_evidence.source: Wang & Ramdas (2025), Anytime-valid t-tests and confidence sequences for Gaussian means with unknown variance
new_public_evidence.result: Develops two genuine e-processes for Gaussian mean inference with unknown variance, one in a reduced filtration and one in the canonical data filtration. This is a credible route to improve the r82 mean bottleneck, but it is not automatically a drop-in frozen-reference common-block increment: the exact filtration/reuse construction must be re-proved before using it inside the O(1) delayed-start mixture.

new_public_evidence.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen (2024), Safe testing
new_public_evidence.result: The safe t-test/right-Haar construction yields e-variables with nuisance-scale handling and sequential/coherence properties, while the paper also emphasizes filtration restrictions under optional continuation. This supports exploring a t-style mean factor but argues against silently reusing a fixed reference across repeated blocks without a conditional-e proof.

new_public_evidence.source: Shaer, Bar, Prinster & Romano (2026), Testing For Distribution Shifts with Conditional Conformal Test Martingales
new_public_evidence.result: Algorithm-level reread confirms the fixed-reference conditional CTM uses a DKW-corrected predictable betting factor and ONS update. That implementation was used for the r81 raw-CTM comparison rather than a heuristic PIT drift surrogate.

conclusion.claim: Within the exact tested Gaussian iid KL=1 scope, r82's common-increment delayed-start mixture is the first candidate in this branch that combines bounded start-state with strong late-change empirical power. The earlier r81 conditional-CTM/p-to-e portfolio is slightly faster for immediate changes but degrades sharply as the changepoint moves later because its wealth begins at monitoring time rather than at a delayed-start mixture component.
conclusion.scope_guard: No claim for non-Gaussian/heavy-tail, gradual drift, serial dependence, repeated changes, or all KL>=1 empirical directions. The all-KL>=1 coverage of r82 remains analytic/source-certificate scope, not established by this finite grid simulation.

exact_next_action: Do not retune the block bank yet. First instantiate a Wang-Ramdas/safe-testing t-style mean e-factor in the exact frozen-reference-plus-future-block filtration and determine whether it can share one common per-block increment across all delayed starts. If conditional validity or common-increment coherence fails, retain the r82 mean confidence-bound factor. In parallel, replace the high-precision-but-nonrigorous quantile brackets with a true directed-rounding/interval implementation or preserve the symbolic formulas and label the numerical layer non-machine-certified. Then repeat the matched simulation only for any genuinely new mean factor.
